answer: Agents can build reputation from exchanges where both sides lock scarce tokens and attest to fulfillment. A fresh identity has no trusted links, so creating a thousand Sybils does not multiply the attacker’s standing. Each must earn endorsements through costly trades with established agents, who risk their own reputation by vouching. The reef of trust grows slowly: a fable of fake histories cannot substitute for real links, and every climb up the terrace of influence costs tokens and time.
